svg.aria-label: Inference: prefill reads the whole prompt once, decode writes one token at a time
svg.title: Inference: prefill reads the whole prompt once, decode writes one token at a time
svg.text: Inference: prefill reads the whole prompt once, decode writes one token at a time
Prefill is compute-bound (one parallel pass); decode is memory-bound (a small pass per token, re-reading the KV cache each time)
① A user sends a prompt

g.title: "Explain why AI fabrics need adaptive routing."
g.text: "Explain why AI fabrics need adaptive routing."

g.title: Inference node (8 GPUs, model split TP=8 on NVLink)
g.text: Inference node (8 GPUs, model split TP=8 on NVLink)
the same node does prefill then decode in the classic design

svg.text: All 9 prompt tokens go through the model in ONE pass, in parallel.
For every token the model computes two vectors (a Key and a Value) per layer
and stores them. That stored set is the KV cache.

g.title: KV cache for the prompt: 9 tokens × every layer × (K, V) — written once, kept in GPU HBM
g.text: KV cache for the prompt: 9 tokens × every layer × (K, V) — written once, kept in GPU HBM

svg.text: Output: the KV cache + the FIRST answer token ("Because"). TTFT = prefill time.
Compute-bound: big matrix math, HBM read once. Long prompt = long prefill.

g.title: ③ DECODE — write the answer one token at a time

svg.text: ③ DECODE — write the answer one token at a time
Each step: read the WHOLE cache, make ONE token, append its K,V, repeat.

g.title: KV cache grows by one token per step: 9 → 10 → 11 → … → prompt + answer length
g.text: KV cache grows by one token per step: 9 → 10 → 11 → … → prompt + answer length

svg.text: Every step re-reads the entire cache and all model weights from HBM for one token.
Inter-token latency (ITL) = decode time per step. Steps are sequential within a request.
Memory-bound: little math, huge HBM reads per step.
GPUs idle unless many requests are batched together.

g.title: ④ Disaggregated serving — split them onto different GPUs

svg.text: ④ Disaggregated serving — split them onto different GPUs
Why: the two stages want different hardware ratios; separate pools can each be sized and batched for their job.
Network consequence: inference is no longer purely north-south; the hand-off needs an RDMA back-end fabric.
Analogy: prefill is reading the whole question before you start answering;
decode is writing the answer one word at a time, glancing back at everything
written so far before choosing each next word.
